hypotheses.statement: The incident was caused by an expired certificate on payments-gateway.internal, which prevented checkout-api from establishing TLS connections to authorize payments.
The release 2026.5.14-a was not the cause of the incident, as it did not modify any code on the checkout submit path.

observed_facts.statement: Release 2026.5.14-a was deployed to production at 09:09:52Z.
At 09:11:47Z, checkout-api payments-connector began experiencing repeated TLS handshake failures to payments-gateway.internal:8443 due to certificate verify failed: certificate has expired.
At 09:12:02Z, POST /v2/checkout/submit began returning 502 upstream_unavailable after payments-connector exhausted retries.
Alert checkout-api-error-ratio fired at 09:12:03Z due to 5xx ratio of 0.184.
Alert checkout-api-latency fired at 09:14:41Z due to p99 latency rising to 10400ms.
INC-7742 was opened at 09:15:00Z with severity 1.
A responder attributed the incident to the release at 09:17:22Z.
A responder disputed the release attribution at 09:23:05Z, pointing to the TLS failures.
At 09:57:55Z, checkout-api payments-connector outbound TLS handshakes to payments-gateway.internal:8443 succeeded again.
A responder from the payments-gateway team reported at 09:59:40Z that the leaf certificate for payments-gateway.internal expired at 09:11:40Z and was rotated at 09:57:50Z.
Rollback of checkout-api to 2026.5.13-c completed at 10:04:18Z, after the 5xx ratio had already recovered.
INC-7742 was marked resolved with a resolution note that only stated 'rolled back and recovered'.

open_questions.missing_evidence: Documentation or automation logs identifying the owner of the certificate renewal automation for payments-gateway.internal.
open_questions.question: Who owns the renewal automation for the payments-gateway.internal certificate?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Impact assessment records or customer communication logs.
open_questions.question: What was the customer impact estimate during the incident?

summary: The checkout-5xx incident was caused by an expired certificate on payments-gateway.internal, which prevented TLS connections for payment authorizations, leading to 502 errors and high latency on POST /v2/checkout/submit. The incident began at 09:11:47Z, recovered after certificate rotation at 09:57:55Z, and was incorrectly attributed to a recent release that did not affect the checkout path. A rollback was performed after recovery, and the resolution note omitted the root cause.

timeline.statement: payments-connector TLS handshake failures begin due to expired certificate.
payments connector recovers after certificate rotation.
INC-7742 marked resolved with incomplete resolution note.
